stem: Hours after the birth of a baby boy, the observant mother noticed that he became cyanotic anytime he cried vigorously. What is the embryological explanation and prognosis for this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: There has been a coarctation of the baby’s aorta

options.label: B
options.text: Vigorous crying opens a patent ductus venosus

options.label: C
options.text: Vigorous crying increases the pressure in the right atrium that temporary opens a yet-to-fuse septum primum

options.label: D
options.text: Surgery is required to correct the defect causing the problem

options.label: E
options.text: Survival rate is very high for babies with this condition

disputed_statements: Transient cyanosis with crying and a prognosis of high survival.
proposed_interpretation: A transient right-to-left atrial shunt is possible if right atrial pressure rises above left atrial pressure. The stem does not establish an isolated patent foramen ovale.
reason: Recurrent visible cyanosis hours after delivery has other serious causes. Prognosis and the need for intervention cannot be inferred from crying alone.

options.label: B
options.text: The blood flow through arteries hit the walls and generate sound at different frequencies

options.label: C
options.text: The narrowing of the blood vessels by the balloon cuff accentuates the sounds already present

options.label: D
options.text: The thick arterial walls vibrate as they get partially occluded

options.label: E
options.text: There is no simple explanation to the use of the equipment

disputed_statements: A
D
reason: The key attributes the audible signal to turbulence, but in vivo ultrafast imaging shows pulse-induced arterial and tissue motion producing the recorded vibration. An alternative specifically mentions arterial wall vibration.
proposed_interpretation: The keyed option reflects a traditional teaching explanation. Arterial wall motion offers a defensible competing answer under current experimental evidence.

disputed_statements: C
D
reason: The keyed capillary hydrostatic pressure drives filtration. Intralymphatic pressure is not an opposing transcapillary Starling force either, so two options could satisfy the exception.

ask_lecturer: Did “closely connected” mean coupling to oxygen binding or a particular spatial contact? Please supply the original slide or structural definition.

paragraphs: Question ID  bio-413  |  Past question
Original stem  The following statements about haemoglobin quaternary structure are true:
A. The α1β2 interface is closely connected to the haem  [F]
B. The α1β2 interface is supposed to be the functional contact area of haemoglobin  [T]
C. Large structural changes take place at the α1β2 interface on oxygenation  [T]
D. The α1β1 interface is a relatively fixed (stabilizing) contact area  [T]

Disputed statement  A — stored false; proposed true if “closely connected” refers to structural or functional coupling rather than literal proximity.

disputed_statements: B
D
E
proposed_interpretation: The mature β-chain sickle substitution is at position 6, near the amino terminus. Experimental inhibitors can mimic either member of a polymer contact.
reason: Kubota and Yang studied peptides representing both the amino-terminal donor region and a proposed complementary contact. The blanket carboxyl-terminal and acceptor-only descriptions cannot cover both examples.

handoff_entry.heading: 03  Biochemistry — anti-sickling peptides
paragraphs: Question ID  bio-428  |  Past question
Original stem  Concerning anti-sickling oligopeptides:
A. They work by dissolving formed HbS fibers  [F]
B. They are synthetic oligopeptides with sequences corresponding to the carboxylterminal region of the βS chain  [T]
C. They are stereo-specific gelation inhibitors of HbS  [T]
D. They resemble the 'sticky patch'  [F]
E. They resemble the 'complementary sites' which develop on deoxyhaemoglobin A or S  [T]

Disputed statements  B, D and E. B is keyed true, but documented experimental peptides include N-terminal sequences. Some inhibitors mimic the donor region, whereas others target the complementary acceptor site.

Ask the lecturer  Which specific class of anti-sickling oligopeptides does the question refer to? Is “carboxylterminal” a transcription error for “amino-terminal”? Should D and E be marked according to a particular peptide design?

Working interpretation  The HbS mutation is β6 Glu→Val, near the amino terminus of the β chain. Deoxygenated HbS polymerises through interactions of this hydrophobic donor region with complementary sites. The mechanism of inhibition depends on the peptide.

Reference: Rational Drug Design of Peptide-Based Therapies for Sickle Cell Disease (2019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6943517/; Stereospecific inhibitors of the gelation of sickle hemoglobin, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7419427/.
